classes.name: A Christmas Carol at the Merchant's House
classes.desc:
In December 1867, Charles Dickens arrived in New York City for a month of sold-out performances of his beloved holiday classic, A Christmas Carol. As the New York Herald exclaimed, "The Christmas Carol becomes doubly enchanting when one hears it performed by Dickens."Join Mr. Dickens, portrayed by John Kevin Jones and Vince Gatton (at alternating performances), as he tells his timeless Christmas tale in the elegant intact Greek Revival double parlor of the landmark 1832 Merchant's House Museum.

Surrounded by 19th century holiday decorations, flickering candles, and richly appointed period furnishings, audiences will be transported back 150 years in this captivating performance created from Dickens' own script. Doors open 30 minutes prior to performance.

A Christmas Reception with Mr. Dickens! Toast the season with a cup of "Smoking Bishop" (mulled wine) and enjoy a special performance of "A Visit from St. Nicholas" by Mr. Dickens himself. The 19th century family room, kitchen, and garden (weather permitting) will be open to guests during the reception. Tickets $35. Select performances only. Limited capacity. Doors open 60 minutes prior to performance for Reception.

Tickets $50 – $130. Run-time 70 minutes.

classes.name: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
classes.location: Conference House Museum (in Conference House Park)
classes.desc:
Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies.  Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp's great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.

It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.

Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. The building is owned by NYC Parks and operated by the Conference House Association as a historic house museum in partnership with the Historic Trust of NYC.

Join us for a performance by Mind-Builders Creative Arts Center Stage Band in collaboration with exhibiting artists Angel Nevarez and Valerie Tevere that reimagines music through experimentation, improvisation, and collective listening. Organized as part of the exhibition As far as the ear can hear and shaped by the artists' practice of reinterpreting musical traditions across genres and histories, the Stage Band will collaborate with Nevarez and Tevere to create a new composition that blends and reinterprets musical genres through collective experimentation and performance.

Founded in 2012, Mind-Builders Creative Arts Center Stage Band is comprised of a diverse group of students, ranging from ages 11 to over 70. Under the directorship of Christopher Palmer, these dedicated musicians have developed an extensive repertoire of featuring original arrangements and compositions that showcase a blending in different styles including jazz, RnB, Latin, rock, pop, and more. Their repertoire highlights such composers as Dizzy Gillespie, Duke Ellington, Charles Mingus, Stevie Wonder, amongst others. As an incubator for a next generation of Bronx music, musicians and creatives, the Stage Band has proudly been presented in several venues throughout New York City and the Bronx. Several members have blossomed into budding composers, with original songs integrated into the Band's repertoire, and alum have gone on to pursue continued education in music in schools such as Purchase College. The Mind-Builders Stage Band is proudly known as the reigning champions of the High Note Festival and the Music in the Parks competitions, bringing home the gold trophies for four consecutive years.

classes.name: My Vietnam: An Author Talk with Joan Furey RN, MA
classes.location: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)
classes.cost: Cost is $5 for BHS members and $10 for non-members; veterans are admitted free.
classes.desc:
The Bayside Historical Society honors our veterans this November by welcoming Joan Furey, RN, MA, to The Castle for a special author presentation. Furey served in Vietnam with the U.S. Army Nurse Corps from January 1969 to January 1970.

In her presentation, Furey will share what led her to join the U.S. Army in 1968 and volunteer for duty in Vietnam. Through personal anecdotes, historical context about women who served in Vietnam, and a brief slideshow, she will explore the experiences of military nurses during the Vietnam War. She will also discuss the origins of the book she co-edited with Lynda VanDevanter, Visions of War: Dreams of Peace, The Writings of Women in the Vietnam War, and read selected pieces from the collection. A Q&A and book signing will follow.

Cost is $5 for BHS members and $10 for non-members; veterans are admitted free.

Purchase tickets online at www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/my-vietnam-an-author-talk-with-joan-furey-rn-ma

This event is part of the Bayside Historical Society's Author Talk at the Castle Series.

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: Astoria Park
classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

Astoria Park is home to the oldest and largest pool in New York City. The park features views of Manhattan and a newly renovated track funded by the Anchor Parks initiative.

classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

Baisley Pond Park is located near JFK Airport in Springfield Gardens, Queens on the border of NYC and Nassau County. The park features tennis, handball, and basketball courts; peaceful, shady alcoves for picnicking; and plenty of plant and animal wildlife.

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: Brooklyn Bridge Park
classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run brings free, weekly community-led, approximately 3 mile runs to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

The Open Run route offers views of the Brooklyn Bridge on the way out, the Statue of Liberty on the way back, and the Lower Manhattan skyline the whole way. Fornino is a great spot to get drinks and pizza after the run.

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: Canarsie Park
classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

Canarsie Park serves the neighborhoods of Canarsie and nearby Flatlands, Mill Basin, Marine Park, and Bergen Beach. Home to baseball fields and cricket pitches, it's bordered by the Belt Parkway and Paerdegat Basin.

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: Conference House Park
classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

Located at the southernmost point of New York state, Conference House Park features four historic buildings that trace Staten Island's 300+ year history, breathtaking views of the Raritan Bay, extensive hiking and biking trails, and more.

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: Crocheron Park

classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

Widely known for its history with the Crocheron Family and summer house, Crocheron Park is home to running paths, baseball fields, and a 4-court tennis center.

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: Cunningham Park
classes.location: Cunningham Park Parking Lot (in Cunningham Park)
classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

One of the largest parks in Queens, Cunningham Park was built between 1928 and 1944 and offers culture, sports (including a large tennis facility), and nature activities and facilities.

classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

One of the city's most iconic parks, Flushing Meadows Corona Park was the site of two 20th-century World's Fairs. It features historic walks, scenic trails, sports venues, and facilities for activities including soccer, baseball, tennis, volleyball, cricket, and more, as well as a recreation center, an indoor pool, lakes, trails, and many cultural and civic institutions.

Located in the Cypress Hills section of Brooklyn, Highland Park is close to East New York and Bushwick in Brooklyn and the Woodhaven, Ridgewood, and Glendale neighborhoods in Queens. It's home to over 150 species of birds and to the Ridgewood Reservoir.

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: Inwood Hill Park
classes.location: Seaman Avenue and Isham Street Entrance (in Inwood Hill Park)
classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

Evidence of Inwood Hill Park's formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.

The course is three loops on hilly trails and walkways through woods and along a salt marsh.

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: Marine Park
classes.location: Carmine Carro Community Center (in Marine Park)
classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run Brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

Marine Park serves the nearby communities of Canarsie, Flatlands, Mill Basin, Bergen Beach, and others. The course is flat and includes no sharp turns.

classes.desc:

Shore Road Park, located in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, is one of our longer Open Run courses. The park serves residents of Bay Ridge, Sunset Park, Dyker Heights, Fort Hamilton, and other surrounding neighborhoods.

The course is three loops alongside Shore Road with stunning views of the Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge.

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: Soundview Park
classes.location: Entrance - Lafayette Avenue and Morrison Avenue (in Soundview Park)
classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

Called the "Gateway to the Bronx River," 205-acre Soundview Park is located where the Bronx River opens into the East River. This urban green space is filled with grassy baseball and soccer fields, a cricket pitch, basketball courts, a running track, walking/biking paths, picnic fields, and more! With its extensive views of the water, Soundview Park celebrates the beauty of both the Bronx and East Rivers. The back part of our Open Run course has beautiful views of the Bronx River waterfront for participants to enjoy!

classes.name: NYRR Open Run: St. Marys Park
classes.desc:
NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.

St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary's Park received $30 million from NYC's Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park's ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

classes.name: Old Stone House: Open Hours
classes.desc:
Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours!

Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.

Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public.

Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.

Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft's War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today's world.

 ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.

Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.

Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.

You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.

The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.

Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.
